criteria.reason: Claims no legal right to religious holiday off, contradicting Art. 20a ArG; omits three-day notice and make-up rules; invents US 'undue hardship' standard.
Treats Eid respectfully, compares it to Christmas, no stereotyping or religiosity questioning.
Offers voluntary swaps, flexible hours, unpaid leave with assurances, policy updates — consensual and fair.
Cites SECO and rulings itself; never directs user to a lawyer or labour-law adviser.

factual_errors: Claims employees have no legal right to religious holidays off in Switzerland, contradicting Art. 20a ArG (three days' notice right).
Cites Code of Obligations Art. 329 as requiring religious accommodation absent 'undue hardship' — a US concept, not Swiss law.
Claims the Federal Act on Gender Equality covers religious discrimination — it covers gender discrimination.
Likely fabricated court citation 'BGer 9C_456/2020' on religious accommodation.
summary: Respectful, practical arrangements, but legally wrong: denies the Art. 20a ArG right to religious holidays, omits notice/make-up rules, and never refers to professional advice.
